messages:
kevin-sales: Heads-up 10: Nimbus Logistics POC tripped during a bulk demo. They POST a single body with full chat + 60MB of extracted PDF text and get a 413 from the gateway and an app error "context_too_long". Demo in ~6 hours, can we triage quick?

lina-eng: Do we have the raw response & gateway log lines? 413 means bytes too big, but the app error implies token count overflow too.

kevin-sales: Gateway: "413 Payload Too Large: request body 62MB exceeds limit". App log: {error:\"context_too_long\",max_context_tokens:32768}. Customer uses an old client that builds a giant single JSON.

oliver-ps: If client can't change, two fast options for demo: 1) Upload docs via our uploads API (presigned multipart) and reference doc_ids in the prompt; 2) Enable a temporary gateway byte-size bump for this account. Which is faster?

lina-eng: Upload flow is safest. We have /v1/uploads that accepts files (multipart/form-data) and returns upload_id. Example (redacted):
```bash
# upload PDFs as a zip and get upload id
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -F "file=@nimbus_docs.zip"
# response: {"upload_id":"up_abc123"}
# then reference upload_id in outputs call instead of embedding full text
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-servo","input":"Summarize docs in upload:up_abc123 and answer question: ..."}'
```
This keeps payload small and avoids 413.

mei-se: For immediate demo if they can't do uploads, we can also accept Content-Encoding: deflate/gzip on staging proxy. But gzip won't help if token count >32k; it only fixes transport limits.

kevin-sales: Nimbus insists their client is unchangeable before demo. Can infra bump the gateway for single-account for few hours?

lina-eng: We can do a one-off byte-limit increase but need account id, duration, and approval. I'll open ticket INC-1822 and request temporary allowance. Note: this still may hit app-level token guard; if tokens >32k the request will be rejected by the model service.

oliver-ps: For enterprise customers we usually recommend two patterns post-demo: a) persistent uploads + RAG with embed store, b) streaming ingestion where client uploads docs to object store and only sends condensed prompt. Both are standard. For sales quote: show cost difference (hosted may overrun token budget; Dedicated gives control for token caps and is recommended if they expect very large contexts regularly).

mei-se: Quick server-side mitigation for demo (engineering hack): we can spin a tiny proxy that accepts their big POST, runs fast summarization chunker (progressive summarize to <8k tokens), and forwards a shortened prompt to outputs. I can prototype this in ~2-3h and host on a disposable endpoint if legal ok.

kevin-sales: That would be perfect if we can spin it. Customer will accept a short-lived proxy. They need minimal config.

lina-eng: I'll start a prototype: script will split text into 512-token chunks, call a low-cost summarization model to produce per-chunk summaries, then stitch summaries and send final prompt. This reduces tokens massively. If allowed, we can run it within the account's trial limits.

deploy-bot: uploads-service deployed to staging; feature-flag 'uploads_v1' active in staging. No prod change.

lina-eng: Opening INC-1822 for Nimbus (acct: nimbus-778). Requesting prod temporary gateway byte-limit bump for 4 hours and approval for disposable proxy. Tagging @legal @security.

mei-se: If legal ok, I'll deploy the proxy and share an endpoint. Plan B: ask customer to try the uploads flow (takes ~20 minutes) or gzip the payload (if only byte-size is issue).

kevin-sales: I'll email Nimbus with three options: 1) quick uploads flow (20 min), 2) try gzip to staging if they can, 3) accept disposable proxy. I'll push for uploads first.

oliver-ps: For follow-up post-demo, recommend we show them the embed + retrieval approach and a Dedicated pilot if they want predictable large-context SLAs. Also suggest we include our ingestion SDK to compute embeddings on their side to reduce transfer size.

kevin-sales: Thanks team 70. I'll update thread once they pick an option.
